name: Self-describing kinetic words

source.description: Three inspected references animate a word the way the word means: STRETCH stretches, SPIN spins, a falling word drops, a word about easing smears.

technique: Each word performs its own meaning, so the motion is the definition. It works because the viewer reads and sees the same idea at once (dual coding) and the treatment never feels arbitrary.
purpose: Make vocabulary memorable; teach motion terms; add wit to kinetic typography.
visual_behaviour: One word per card; the letters stretch, spin, drop, snap to guides, echo or slide in a way that enacts the word.
mechanics: Short single-property tweens (scaleX, rotation, per-character y with seeded rotation, letter-spacing) of 0.3-0.6 s with expressive eases (expo.out, back.out); outlined echo copies for repetition words.

decomposition.timing: One word per 0.5-1.5 s in the references; each treatment resolves within about 60% of its card.

parameters.name: treatment
parameters.description: rise | smear | drop | stretch | spin | track | echo | cut

failure_modes: Treatment that contradicts the word (a slow 'snap')
Using it for words that have no motion meaning
Mixing too many treatments in one line of copy

implementation.approach: Treatments of Studio.comp.wordBeats (rise, smear, drop, stretch, spin, track, echo, cut); other verbs compose existing effects.

limitations: Snap-to-guide and squash-word treatments are not built in; compose them from guide lines and Studio.space.bounce

provenance.observed: Single verbs on cards: a heavy word drops, STRETCH is stretched wide, SPIN rotates, SNAP lands on drawn guide lines.
A word about easing arrives stretched and smeared; NEVER falls in letter by letter and then tiles the frame.
BOLD. is stacked with outlined echo copies above and below.

evidence.notes: Contact sheet inspected: RISE, RUSH, DROP, WIDEN, TURN, SPACE, REPEAT, STOP each perform their meaning.
Fold squeezes in from a 1.7x stretch, Crease tightens its tracking, Fly smears in (stretch lowered so frame 0 stays inside portrait and square). Frame review 0 errors, 0 warnings (preview grade).

licensing_notes: Technique only, learned from user-supplied references (inspiration-only, rights unknown). Word list in the test is original.
